name: Tujia, Southern dialect / 土家语南部方言, Poluozhai 婆落寨 variety

catalog_citation: Zhang, Jun 张军. 2006. Tujiayu yuyin yanjiu 土家语语音研究 [A phonological study of the Tujia language]. PhD thesis, Division of Humanities, Hong Kong University of Science and Technology. hdl:1783.1/2836 (open repository PDF).
catalog_quote: 三．声调（5） 表16—南部方言声调（5）［调类／调值］：高降调 53；高升调 45；中平调 33；低升调 13；低降调 21。声调举例：i53 远近之远 se53 栽种之栽；i45 有无之有 se45 诅咒之骂；i33 山寨之寨 se33 赊欠之赊；i13 流动之流 se13 粪便之屎；i21 移动之移 se21 死亡之死。声调说明：（1）高降调53有55、53两个变体，在听感上是一个短促调，类似汉语方言中无塞音韵尾的入声调。（2）高升45的实际调值为445。（3）低升13调的实际调值常常为24。（4）低降21调可以读为22或11。（5）声调连读变化相对自由，可随音节的走向而定。 [p. 193] 北部方言各点均有四个声调，以龙山县坡脚乡多谷村为代表；南部方言有五个声调，以泸溪县潭溪乡婆落寨为代表。本章材料均为笔者调查。 [Translation: III. Tones (5). Table 16, tones of the Southern dialect (5): high falling 53; high rising 45; mid level 33; low rising 13; low falling 21. Tone examples: i53 'far', se53 'plant'; i45 'have', se45 'curse'; i33 'stockade village', se33 'owe'; i13 'flow', se13 'excrement'; i21 'move', se21 'die'. Notes on the tones: (1) the high falling 53 has two variants 55 and 53; auditorily it is a short abrupt tone, like the entering tone without stop coda of Chinese dialects. (2) The actual value of high rising 45 is 445. (3) The actual value of low rising 13 is often 24. (4) Low falling 21 may be read 22 or 11. (5) Tone change in connected speech is relatively free and may follow the drift of the syllables. p. 193: Every Northern point has four tones, represented by Duogu village, Pojiao township, Longshan county; the Southern dialect has five tones, represented by Poluozhai, Tanxi township, Luxi county. All material in this chapter is the author's own fieldwork.]
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.quote: 三．声调（5） 表16—南部方言声调（5）[table linearised]：高降调 53；高升调 45；中平调 33；低升调 13；低降调 21。……声调说明：（1）高降调53有55、53两个变体，在听感上是一个短促调，类似汉语方言中无塞音韵尾的入声调。（2）高升45的实际调值为445。（3）低升13调的实际调值常常为24。（4）低降21调可以读为22或11。（5）声调连读变化相对自由，可随音节的走向而定。
new_statements.translation: III. Tones (5). Table 16 — Tones of the Southern dialect (5): high falling 53; high rising 45; mid level 33; low rising 13; low falling 21. ... Notes on the tones: (1) The high falling tone 53 has two variants, 55 and 53; auditorily it is a short, abrupt tone, similar to the entering tone without a stop coda in Chinese dialects. (2) The actual pitch value of the high rising 45 is 445. (3) The actual value of the low rising 13 tone is often 24. (4) The low falling 21 tone may be pronounced 22 or 11. (5) Tone changes in connected speech are relatively free and may depend on the drift of the syllables.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Southern Tujia is a tone language with five lexical tones on every syllable (53, 45, 33, 13, 21 in the Poluozhai variety); the description gives no rule for word stress and never mentions stress, prominence or neutral tone for the Southern dialect. No stress placement can be stated.
new_statements.exceptions: None about stress. The author notes tone sandhi in connected speech is 'relatively free'. A separate passage on the NORTHERN dialect (§8.1.5, pp. 228-229) says neutralised final syllables are not weaker in intensity or shorter, and that any neutral-tone-like weakening would be in initial or medial syllables of polysyllabic words (as in Jingpho, Dulong); this is not about Southern Tujia.
new_statements.domain_note: Citation-form monosyllabic tones of the Poluozhai 婆落寨 village variety (Tanxi township, Luxi County), from the author's own fieldwork 2002-2004; the note (5) concerns connected speech. Zhou 2020 (pp. 30-31, from Li 2000 and Xiang 2017) reports the same five-tone system for Xiadu and Qieji as /55/ (~53), /33/ (~31), /35/, /21/, /13/.
new_statements.identity_note: Zhang 2006's Southern data are the Poluozhai 婆落寨 village variety of Tanxi township, Luxi County (author's fieldwork 2002-2004); Zhou 2020's CB = Xiadu 下都 (Li 2000) and CJ = Qieji 且己 (Xiang 2017). All are Southern Tujia / Mengzi (Mongrzzirhof, autonym /mõ21 dzɿ21/) = sout2739 [tjs]. Zhang 2006's stress-adjacent §8.1.5 remark concerns the Northern dialect of Duogu, Longshan (Northern Tujia [tji], a different glottocode), not sout2739.

sources.citation: Zhou, Yulou. 2020. Proto-Bizic: A study of Tujia historical phonology. B.A. honors thesis, Department of Linguistics, Stanford University (supervisors Paul Kiparsky, Dominic Yu). 141 pp. ('computer-friendly version with typographical corrections'; also the 142-pp. official submitted version)
sources.note: No statement on stress or accent anywhere (a full-text search for stress/accent/prominence). Synchronic sketch of Southern Tujia pp. 30-31: 'The five monosyllabic tones of CB [Xiadu, from Li 2000] are /55/ ([55] and [53] as free variants), /33/ ([33] and [31] as free variants), /35/, /21/, /13/ with CJ [Qieji, from Xiang 2017] tones in parentheses. 13 and 21 are sometimes indistinguishable in normal speech (Xiang 2017:38)'; Table 5-2 (p. ~92) notes that all past research (Li 2000, Xiang 2017, Tian 1986) agrees Southern Tujia has five distinctive tones. Historical reconstruction only otherwise.
